claims.text: Al and Cr are reactive elements capable of forming stable oxides.
Increasing oxide-forming elements in an HEA will promote formation of a stable protective oxide film under high-temperature tribo-corrosion conditions.
The protective oxide film will give the tailored HEA superior degradation resistance relative to traditional alloys.
The proposed initial material is a conventional HEA or traditional structural alloy not optimized for oxide-film formation.
Increasing the proportion of oxide-forming elements will promote in situ development of a protective, stable oxide layer.
The proposed dense and adherent surface oxide film will reduce further oxidation.
The proposed dense and adherent surface oxide film will reduce wear.
The tailored elemental mixture will promote rapid formation of an intrinsically stable passivation layer during exposure.
The passivation layer will act as a barrier against corrosion.
The passivation layer will act as a barrier against abrasion.
The tailored HEA will have lower weight loss than conventional structural alloys and untailored HEAs under identical tribo-corrosion conditions.
The tailored HEA will have improved wear resistance relative to conventional structural alloys and untailored HEAs under identical tribo-corrosion conditions.
The tailored HEA will sustain less corrosion damage than conventional structural alloys and untailored HEAs under identical tribo-corrosion conditions.
The enhanced resistance will be effective only in environments combining significant high-temperature stresses with tribo-corrosive forces.
The proposed benefits may not be observable under less aggressive or non-oxidative conditions.
